builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization
summary: EDAGoat replaces manual expert tuning of GPU-accelerated EDA tools with an LLM coding agent that applies four cross-project optimization patterns (OE mode) and enforces correctness and design-quality checks on all public and hidden inputs before a search qualifies (MV mode). It costs agent API calls across three independent searches per project, requires an executable validation harness covering EDA constraints, and adds orchestration complexity relative to single-pass prompting. Without mandatory validation, agents frequently produce edits that fail correctness or design-quality checks (DeepSeek generic prompting qualified in only 7 of 15 searches), and the results are demonstrated only on five EDA projects with frontier API models, so transfer to other GPU codebases is unverified.
rationale: The method targets GPU-accelerated EDA tools, a domain outside typical ML production work, but its validated-search agent pattern is worth monitoring as it matures for general code optimization.
technique: EDA-aware agentic GPU code optimization with mandatory validation

claims.statement: EDAGoat replaces manual expert tuning of GPU-accelerated EDA tools with an LLM coding agent that applies four cross-project optimization patterns (OE mode) and enforces correctness and design-quality checks on all public and hidden inputs before a search qualifies (MV mode). It costs agent API calls across three independent searches per project, requires an executable validation harness covering EDA constraints, and adds orchestration complexity relative to single-pass prompting. Without mandatory validation, agents frequently produce edits that fail correctness or design-quality checks (DeepSeek generic prompting qualified in only 7 of 15 searches), and the results are demonstrated only on five EDA projects with frontier API models, so transfer to other GPU codebases is unverified.

With DeepSeek, mandatory validation plus EDA-aware optimization patterns raises the geometric mean of per-project mean speedups from 1.11x (generic prompting) to 1.53x, and qualifies 13 of 15 searches versus 7 of 15; with GPT-6 Astra it qualifies 15 of 15 and reaches 1.57x versus 1.26x.
